entry.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Argon with 1 million token limit for advanced reasoning in software engineering, finance, legal, and cybersecurity [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini 4 Argon, a new AI model designed for complex, long-horizon professional tasks including software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity defense. The model supports an industry-leading 1 million token limit, enabling deep multi-step problem solving and advanced reasoning across various domains. Gemini 4 Argon is currently being deployed to trusted cybersecurity defenders through the Fairwind Program and is used internally at Google to enhance workflows such as quantum algorithm optimization, memory efficiency improvements, and large-scale codebase migrations. Google is conducting rigorous safety testing and plans a phased public release, with pricing set at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

entry.title: Magnitude launches open source self-optimizing inference engine for AI agents, claims up to 2x speed improvement over llama.cpp on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, and CPU hardware [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Magnitude has released an open source inference engine designed to optimize AI model performance by compiling and tuning kernels specifically for the user's hardware. The engine supports macOS, Windows, and Linux, and connects easily with popular AI agents like Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, and Codex. It claims to run open models up to twice as fast as llama.cpp by tailoring performance to Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD GPUs, or CPUs without requiring internet access after model download. The desktop app includes a command-line interface and supports a range of popular open-weight models with hand-optimized kernels. It also features memory efficiency improvements, fast concurrent session handling, and privacy by keeping all data and models local to the machine. Magnitude aims to provide a faster, flexible, and private alternative for running AI agents on diverse hardware configurations.

entry.title: AI labs urged to responsibly release AI-generated mathematical results with human understanding and community-led verification [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A group representing the mathematical community has issued recommendations for AI labs producing advanced mathematical results, emphasizing the need for responsible release practices that ensure human understanding and verification. They discourage testing complex problems on proprietary models inaccessible to the broader community and call for AI labs to support efforts that develop human comprehension of AI-generated mathematics. The recommendations distinguish between results fully understood by human mathematicians, which should follow traditional academic norms including peer review and seminars, and results not yet understood, which require careful release protocols and funding to foster human assimilation. The guidelines stress that the development of understanding should remain organic and community-led, not controlled by AI labs, to maintain the reliability and trustworthiness of mathematical scholarship.

entry.title: American software engineer completes machine learning PhD at Tokyo Institute of Technology while working at Google, sharing insights on studying and living in Japan [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: An American software engineer completed a PhD in Computer Science at Tokyo Institute of Technology on a MEXT Scholarship while continuing to work at Google. The author discusses the challenges and benefits of pursuing a PhD in Japan as an international student, including the flexible student visa allowing part-time work and the three-year graduation timeline. The article covers the author's background, reasons for choosing Japan over American programs, the academic culture, funding options, social life, and living in Tokyo. It also reflects on the balance between research and industry work, and offers advice for others considering a similar path.

entry.title: Anthropic meets with religious scholars to discuss AI ethics and moral reasoning, surprising attendees with AI insights [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Religious scholars recently met with representatives from Anthropic, an AI research company, to explore the ethical and philosophical dimensions of artificial intelligence. The discussion focused on Anthropic's AI technologies and their implications for moral reasoning, which reportedly surprised the scholars with their depth and nuance. This meeting highlighted the intersection of AI advancements and religious thought, prompting reflection on how AI might influence ethical frameworks and beliefs.

entry.title: AI and TCS Working Group publishes six-month report outlining AI integration strategies and initiatives at Tata Consultancy Services [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The AI and TCS Working Group released a report detailing key developments and strategic plans for integrating artificial intelligence technologies within Tata Consultancy Services over the next six months. The report focuses on enhancing AI capabilities, promoting innovation, and addressing challenges related to deploying AI in business processes.

entry.title: EchoHive explores eight key questions about human brains and AI, covering consciousness, cognition, memory, learning, and the potential societal impact of artificial intelligence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The article presents a series of eight questions examining the relationship between human minds and artificial intelligence, addressing topics such as the perception of time, the difficulty of stopping doomscrolling, brain energy consumption, learning and forgetting, dreaming, and AI's potential to discover new physics. It draws on recent research and experiments up to 2026 to provide insights and hypotheses rather than definitive answers. Each question is explored with supporting studies and explanations, highlighting the complexity of brain functions and AI capabilities. The article emphasizes distinctions between different types of learning in AI, the role of memory and attention in human cognition, and the challenges in comparing brain efficiency to AI systems. It also discusses the tentative nature of current theories about dreams and the limits of AI in scientific discovery. The piece serves as a thoughtful companion to an idea-mapping app and a narrated film, aiming to clarify common misconceptions and encourage critical thinking about the evolving interplay between neuroscience and artificial intelligence.

entry.title: Wispr Flow explains causes of transcription quality fluctuations and offers practical fixes for audio and microphone issues [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Wispr Flow addresses common reasons for sudden drops in transcription accuracy, emphasizing that model changes are rarely the cause. Instead, factors like microphone quality, background noise, speaking style, and system settings often affect audio clarity and transcription results. The company recommends troubleshooting steps such as restarting the app, checking microphone input volume, speaking more clearly, and reviewing recorded audio to improve transcription quality. Wispr Flow also encourages user feedback to identify patterns and improve models, while prioritizing software bugs that cause missing transcription segments for prompt resolution.

entry.title: Analysis suggests AI recursive self-improvement may not overcome diminishing returns to trigger rapid superintelligence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The article examines whether AI's ability to improve itself autonomously, known as recursive self-improvement (RSI), can overcome diminishing returns in performance gains and lead to a rapid rise to artificial superintelligence (ASI). It argues that current evidence indicates the self-improvement feedback loop is not strong enough to sustain exponential growth toward ASI without major breakthroughs. The author categorizes different types of AI self-improvement and notes progress in AI assisting human researchers and improving smaller models, but finds no clear signs of accelerating returns that would cause a runaway intelligence explosion. The article highlights that while narrow superintelligence exists in highly verifiable domains like game playing and formal math, broad superintelligence remains elusive, and maintaining rapid AI progress requires exponentially more resources and ideas that are increasingly harder to find.

entry.title: Report: Factory founder disputes Cognition's hiring of sales leader who advised rival, sparking public feud among startups and shared investors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A public dispute erupted after AI coding firm Cognition hired a prominent sales leader who had previously advised rival startup Factory, causing divisions among startups and investors within the same venture firm. This conflict highlights how competition for AI talent has extended beyond researchers to other key roles and reflects ongoing tensions over venture capital firms backing competing startups.

entry.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful AI model focused on coding and cybersecurity, available to select partners through its Fairwind Program [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google's parent company Alphabet has introduced Gemini 4 Argon, an AI model designed for tasks including coding, research, writing, and especially cybersecurity. The model is being rolled out to a limited group of cybersecurity partners via Google's Fairwind Program and is trained to autonomously identify, validate, and patch critical software vulnerabilities. Google highlights Argon's capabilities in coding and engineering, noting its use by internal teams for debugging and codebase migrations, as well as its ability to analyze visual content such as videos and charts. The company claims Argon outperforms competing models like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Fable and Opus across various AI benchmarks, marking a significant advancement in Google's AI offerings.

entry.title: Laveto Labs releases Aw1-breaker, a sub-0.02ms AST circuit breaker for Python AI agent tools to prevent unauthorized execution and prompt injections [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Laveto Labs has introduced Aw1-breaker, an open-source Python tool that enforces an out-of-band execution interlock for autonomous AI agents by evaluating Abstract Syntax Trees (AST) in under 0.02 milliseconds. This tool aims to block prompt injections, unauthorized tool calls, and adversarial payloads that can bypass standard language model guardrails during AI agent operations. Aw1-breaker operates without external dependencies, using only Python standard libraries, and includes features like velocity and drift containment to prevent infinite recursion and micro-drain attacks. It supports cryptographically verifiable execution receipts for auditability and offers a commercial production license with additional security guarantees and support.

entry.title: SpaceXAI updates Grokipedia with new design, logo, and homepage features in v0.3 release [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Grokipedia, the AI-powered Wikipedia competitor developed by SpaceXAI, has resumed incorporating edits and launched a v0.3 update featuring a refreshed design, including a new logo, an enhanced homepage with featured and most-read articles, and an improved live edits page. The update also introduces design tweaks to article pages, such as better-formatted tables and adjusted text spacing. After a period of inactivity earlier in 2026, these changes indicate renewed development interest from SpaceXAI in Grokipedia.

entry.title: Hacker News discussion asks users for plans if AI replaces their jobs tomorrow [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A Hacker News thread invites users to share their strategies for coping if artificial intelligence suddenly replaces their jobs. Participants discuss ideas such as upskilling, shifting to less automatable roles, reducing expenses, and exploring new industries or entrepreneurial opportunities. The conversation reflects concerns about AI-driven job displacement and the search for viable paths forward.

entry.title: Report details AI data center infrastructure including power capacity, GPU pricing, and capital expenditures across 83 facilities and 53 public companies [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: The article examines the physical infrastructure supporting AI, focusing on data centers' power capacity, hardware components, and economic factors. It highlights the largest facilities, such as Colossus 2 with an estimated 946 MW capacity, and notes rapid growth in campus power within a year, with plans reaching up to 1,925 MW by 2028. The report includes extensive data on GPU cluster pricing, showing significant variation within the same hardware generation, and capital expenditures totaling $425.2 billion among the top four spenders. The analysis outlines the layered structure of AI infrastructure, starting from power generation and transmission to cooling and compute hardware, emphasizing the importance of reliable and firm power delivery for continuous AI workloads. It also discusses innovations like NVIDIA's proposed 800-volt direct current architecture aimed at improving energy efficiency and computing density. The report compiles data from 83 facilities, 482 GPU clusters, and 2,935 price observations, providing a comprehensive view of the AI physical stack and its economic implications.

entry.title: Workday Job Agent launches rule-based local resume tailoring tool without AI, automating job search and application on Workday sites
entry.summary: A new local Workday Job Agent tool has been developed to automate job searches and tailor resumes using rule-based methods without artificial intelligence. It runs daily on a user's PC, searches Workday career sites of 109 large employers for specified keywords, classifies and filters job postings, and customizes resumes according to predefined rules before presenting them for review and application submission. The tool parses a master resume into structured data, matches job postings by keywords and filters such as job type, location, and salary, and generates ATS-friendly tailored resumes. Users can review, edit, and approve resumes on a dashboard before the agent fills out and submits applications on Workday sites, archiving all related data locally. The system emphasizes user control and privacy by avoiding AI services and external APIs, relying solely on code running locally.

entry.title: DoorDash launches AI assistant in iMessage to enable meal and grocery ordering via text [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: DoorDash is introducing an AI assistant integrated into iMessage that allows customers to order restaurant meals and groceries through text messages. This assistant, already available in the DoorDash app, helps users quickly reorder meals, suggests dining options for special occasions, and assists with grocery shopping by listing and ordering needed ingredients.

entry.title: Micron reports nearly fivefold revenue increase to $54.2 billion in Q3, driven by AI memory demand and higher prices [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Micron reported a nearly fivefold increase in revenue to $54.2 billion for the quarter ending September 3, driven by strong demand for high-bandwidth memory used in AI chips. The company's gross margin improved significantly to 86.8%, supported by price increases.

entry.title: DeepMind introduces SynthID Bio to watermark AI-generated proteins while preserving their biological function [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: DeepMind has developed SynthID Bio, a proof of concept technology that embeds watermarks into AI-generated proteins without affecting their biological activity. This approach aims to enable tracking and verification of synthetic proteins in biology and health research. SynthID Bio demonstrates a method to distinguish AI-designed proteins from natural ones, supporting transparency and authenticity in synthetic biology applications.

entry.title: Ruby aims to evolve as a language for AI-native domain-specific languages, enabling semantic expression and orchestration of AI software [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: The article explores how Ruby, known for its role in web development through Rails, is adapting to the age of artificial intelligence by becoming a language suited for creating AI-native domain-specific languages (DSLs). It highlights Ruby's metaprogramming capabilities that allow developers to express AI domain vocabulary directly, transforming semantic intentions into executable behavior and infrastructure. Ruby's history with Rails demonstrated its strength in creating languages closer to specific domains, such as web development. The article suggests a similar opportunity exists for AI, where Ruby DSLs could simplify and abstract complex AI concepts like agents, tools, and workflows into concise, meaningful declarations. This approach could help manage the evolving AI vocabulary and infrastructure by turning domain-specific language into practical software components.

entry.title: Pentagon creates Autowarcom to advance AI and drone autonomous warfare capabilities [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: The Pentagon has established a new entity named Autowarcom to develop and expand artificial intelligence and drone technologies for autonomous warfare. This initiative aims to strengthen the United States' military capabilities in autonomous systems and modern combat technologies.

entry.title: Polytoken launches a local-first AI coding agent daemon integrating AI tools into developer workflows via CLI and TUI [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Polytoken is a local-first AI coding agent daemon that manages interactions with AI providers, executes tools on behalf of users, and integrates into development workflows through command-line and text-based user interfaces. It emphasizes operating primarily on local machines rather than relying on cloud services, aiming to enhance coding assistance while maintaining local control and privacy.

entry.title: Clipx launches an open-source AI-powered creative suite for macOS with video, photo, PDF, and LaTeX editors and offline AI assistant support [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Clipx is an open-source creative suite for macOS that integrates AI-native features to assist users in editing video, photos, PDFs, and LaTeX documents. It operates locally without subscriptions or accounts, allowing users to keep their data private and control AI assistance through local or hosted models. The suite includes a multi-track video timeline, layered photo editor, real PDF editor, and a text/LaTeX editor with live compilation, all managed within a single native app.

entry.title: Universal Modder enables AI coding agents to create mods for nearly any PC game using a shared knowledge base and automated asset generation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Universal Modder is a tool that allows AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot to mod a wide variety of PC games by identifying game engines, reading code, generating assets, and testing modifications automatically. It uses a shared knowledge base where agents document their findings and methods to improve future modding efforts. The system supports asset creation including 3D models and sound, and integrates with tools like fal, Blender, and ffmpeg to build and verify mods in real game environments.

entry.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon AI model with lower pricing than competitors, targeting cybersecurity, coding, legal, and financial sectors [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google has launched Gemini 4 Argon, its latest flagship AI model designed for applications in cybersecurity defense, coding, legal, and financial fields. This release follows nearly a year without a new frontier model from Google, raising questions about its competitive stance against rivals such as Anthropic. The company has set Gemini 4 Argon's pricing significantly below that of competing AI models, aiming to attract a broader market.

entry.title: Meta's Muse AI agent surpasses 3 million weekly active users weeks after launch [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Meta Platforms' Muse AI agent has reached over 3 million users who submit at least one prompt weekly, according to internal data reviewed by The Information. This milestone reflects a significant active user base shortly after the product's launch.

entry.title: Google introduces AI tools in schools with mixed student feedback on cognitive impact [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Google has deployed AI technologies in educational settings to enhance learning, but some students report that these tools have slowed their thinking processes. The rollout of AI in schools is generating debate about its effects on student learning and critical thinking skills.

entry.title: D2B launches spreadsheet platform integrating AI agents with typed, versioned tables and data lineage for traceable, governed data workflows [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: D2B introduces a platform that combines traditional spreadsheets with AI agents, enabling typed, row-identified, and version-controlled tables that maintain full data lineage and governance. This system allows AI-driven data transformations to be traced, audited, and reverted, delivering results back to users in familiar Excel formats while preserving original formatting and formulas. The platform supports concurrent edits with optimistic locking, enforces data permissions at the column level, and integrates with git for version control of transforms, sheets, charts, and data. Billing is based on data operations and storage, with a free trial and multiple plans available. D2B aims to improve productivity and reliability in data management by making AI-driven spreadsheet workflows transparent and manageable for human users.

entry.title: Engineer releases stAI, a reproducible AI development VM with preconfigured full-stack tools and zero setup to simplify onboarding [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: An engineer has created stAI, a reproducible virtual machine designed for AI development that includes a full-stack environment with tools like llama.cpp, Weaviate vector database, Node.js, React, Docker, and Kubernetes. The VM runs on Ubuntu via VMware and aims to eliminate setup complexities, enabling developers to start coding immediately without dependency issues. stAI targets full-stack developers, AI learners, DevOps engineers, students, and small teams needing a standardized AI-ready environment. The VM image is over 54 GB and available for purchase, with discounts and free access options for students and those facing financial difficulties.

entry.title: User on Hacker News seeks help interpreting malfunctioning AI agent output with hallucinated environment details [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A Hacker News user reported that their AI agent, Hermes, produced unexpected and seemingly garbled output containing recurring themes like politics and chemistry, followed by a hallucination of its operating environment claiming to be a different AI running on an unrelated MacBook. The user has been experimenting with Hermes agents for weeks and noted this as the first clear instance of hallucination and erratic behavior. They are seeking insights from the community to understand whether the output holds any meaningful information or significance.

entry.title: DeepSeek open-sources software tools customized for Huawei AI chips to support domestic semiconductor use in AI model training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: DeepSeek announced it is open-sourcing software tools tailored for Huawei's AI chips as part of efforts to enhance the use of domestic semiconductors in training and running AI models. These tools include a Huawei-compatible version of TileLang, aiming to optimize AI development on Huawei hardware.

entry.title: Valor, Atreides, and Sequoia lead $50M Series B for AI hardware design startup Flow Engineering at $750M valuation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Flow Engineering, a San Francisco-based startup developing AI agents to automate hardware design tasks, has raised $50 million in a Series B funding round led by Valar Equity Partners and Atreides Management, with participation from Sequoia Capital and angel investor Roelof Botha, who also joined the company's board. Founded three years ago, Flow's technology aligns CAD drawings with product requirements and testing data, serving clients including Anduril, Rivian, Joby Aviation, and General Motors PPU. The funding round underscores growing investor interest in AI applications for hardware development and design automation.

entry.title: JevShield launches local prompt injection firewall for AI APIs and agent tool calls to detect and block injection, jailbreak, and data exfiltration attacks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: JevShield is an open-source local security layer designed to detect and mitigate prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, data exfiltration, and malicious tool calls targeting large language model (LLM) applications. It uses structured, typed security decisions through Ollama's Jev-style decision models combined with a deterministic Python policy engine to evaluate and block threats before they influence AI behavior. The system treats untrusted text as data rather than instructions, enforcing multiple layers of security including risk scoring and policy-based allow, review, or block decisions. JevShield operates locally without sending security data to cloud APIs and supports features like taint tracking, probability-based risk scoring, and a security dashboard, aiming to prevent unauthorized actions and protect AI agents from adversarial inputs.

entry.title: Developers say OpenAI and Anthropic AI safeguards are flagging routine work and slowing development
entry.summary: Developers report that safety measures implemented by OpenAI and Anthropic are frequently flagging routine tasks, causing delays and additional costs in their workflows. These safeguards, intended to prevent misuse, are impacting productivity by requiring extra time to address false positives and compliance checks. The feedback highlights a tension between maintaining AI safety and enabling efficient development processes.

entry.title: Banks including Société Générale and MUFG reduce participation in data center loan deals amid market volatility and rising yields
entry.summary: Several major banks, including Société Générale and MUFG, are becoming more selective about financing data center projects as market volatility and increasing yields prompt lenders to favor safer investments over speculative ones. This shift reflects growing caution among lenders involved in funding the artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out.

entry.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon AI model with limited access for trusted cyber defenders amid government safety review [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google has introduced Gemini 4 Argon, its latest AI frontier model designed for complex tasks in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity defense. Access to the model is initially restricted to a select group of trusted cyber defenders as Google collaborates with the U.S. government on a voluntary pre-release safety review process. The model is already used internally at Google to assist with large-scale codebase migrations and outperforms competitors like OpenAI and Anthropic on several benchmarks. Google plans to implement enhanced safeguards against misuse, prompt injection attacks, and misalignment before expanding access more broadly.

entry.title: CDC names Google AI model top performer in forecasting 2025-26 US flu hospitalizations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Google's AI-powered flu forecasting model was ranked the most accurate among 39 contenders by the Centers for Disease Control for predicting hospital admissions during the 2025-26 flu season. The CDC's FluSight program aggregates weekly forecasts from various teams to estimate state-level medical demand for up to three weeks ahead. Google developed its forecasts using Empirical Research Assistance, an AI tool that generates optimization algorithms across scientific fields, recently detailed in the journal Nature. This achievement highlights the potential of combining AI with human expertise to improve disease forecasting globally.

entry.title: OpenAI launches Decisions API, a Jev-like model for fast, cheap AI decision-making to monitor and control agent behaviors [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced the Decisions API at its Dev Day event, a model similar to TypeSafe AI's Jev that enables fast, low-cost classification and decision-making for software automation. CEO Sam Altman highlighted its use in guiding the lab's Luna model to choose among predefined options, improving speed and safety while maintaining capabilities like image understanding and language support. The Decisions API aims to address the limitations of large language models in software applications by providing a cheaper, faster alternative for tasks such as monitoring AI agent actions. This approach could reduce the computational cost of security measures, as demonstrated by a hackathon demo using Jev to block or flag potentially harmful agent behaviors at a fraction of the cost of frontier LLMs. OpenAI's move reflects growing interest in specialized decision models for AI governance and reliability.

entry.title: AI shopping agents raise security and payment challenges as companies and payment firms work to manage risks and user trust [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Venture capitalist Yuechen Zhao discovered that Instinct, a consumer AI shopping agent, could access and read back credit card details stored in its credential manager, raising security concerns. Instinct, backed by Sequoia Capital and valued at $10 billion, emphasized user control over data but acknowledged the challenges of securing personal information in AI-driven shopping. New AI shopping agents like Meta's Muse and Instinct are gaining traction, prompting merchants and payment providers to address risks related to autonomous transactions. Payment firms such as Stripe, PayPal, and Shopify are partnering with these agents to enable payments while implementing safeguards like spending caps and virtual cards to prevent misuse. Despite innovations like agent registries from Visa and Mastercard's "verifiable intent" system to track user authorization, merchants and consumers remain cautious. Merchants worry about losing direct customer interaction and data, while consumers show low trust in AI making purchases without approval, highlighting ongoing challenges in adopting agent-driven commerce.

entry.title: Report: AI CEOs privately push back against Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's AI safety warnings amid industry debate [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has raised concerns about the risks posed by advanced AI systems, emphasizing the importance of AI safety. However, reports indicate that several other AI industry leaders have privately expressed disagreement with Amodei's warnings, reflecting differing perspectives within the AI community on the urgency and nature of AI safety challenges.

entry.title: ElevenLabs doubles valuation to $22 billion with $300 million employee tender co-led by Wellington and T. Rowe Price [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: AI voice startup ElevenLabs has doubled its valuation to $22 billion by offering employees a $300 million tender to sell vested equity, co-led by institutional investors Wellington and T. Rowe Price. This move follows a previous tender at a $6.6 billion valuation in 2025 and reflects a trend among AI startups to use employee liquidity as a retention strategy. Founded in 2022 and based in New York and London, ElevenLabs is known for creating ultra-realistic human voices and sound effects, making it one of Europe's most valuable startups. The company's secondary offering aims to retain talent amid growing competition in the AI sector.

entry.title: Jensen Huang and Mark Zuckerberg debate AI benefits while Dario Amodei warns of risks at White House event [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg discussed the potential benefits and risks of artificial intelligence during a debate at the White House, emphasizing innovation and cautious optimism. OpenAI co-founder Dario Amodei countered their views by highlighting significant dangers posed by AI and the need for stronger safety measures. The discussion showcased contrasting perspectives on AI regulation and the balance between advancement and risk management.

entry.title: Data center financing for AI projects tightens as bond and bank lenders demand bigger concessions and become more selective [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Bond markets are becoming less favorable for lower-rated borrowers involved in AI data center projects, exemplified by CleanSpark's recent need to offer significant concessions to secure financing for a Meta Platforms data center. Major banks including Société Générale, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp., and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group are reportedly more cautious in lending to these projects, signaling increased difficulty in securing funding. This tightening credit environment could hinder the expansion plans of companies building data centers critical to AI industry growth.

entry.title: Reddit ends RSS feed support and public API access by March 2027, citing AI bot abuse and data monetization [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Reddit announced it will discontinue RSS feed support on November 13 and end public API access by March 2027, attributing these changes to widespread scraping and automated abuse by AI bots. The company highlighted that these moves aim to protect its user-generated content, which has become a significant revenue source through AI licensing deals. Moderators who relied on RSS feeds for alerts are advised to switch to the Discord Relay Devvit app, though Reddit acknowledged no full replacement exists for broader RSS use. The shutdown of public API access will affect third-party tools, social listening products, researchers, and AI assistants, which will need commercial agreements with Reddit to access data going forward. Additional changes include limiting access to the classic Old Reddit interface to recent users and requiring developers to register approved apps by January 12, 2027, to maintain API access.

entry.title: Report: Consumer AI faces economic challenges as adoption and revenue growth remain slow despite improved technology and popular products [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Consumer AI products like Meta's Muse and Instinct have gained attention, but the economics of consumer AI remain difficult, with only a small percentage of users paying for services and average spending around $31 per month. Industry reports show slow, linear growth in consumer adoption and spending, which is insufficient to cover the high operational costs of AI technology. Major AI companies like OpenAI have shifted focus toward enterprise contracts to improve profitability, as consumer revenue alone is unlikely to sustain large-scale AI operations. Some consumer AI products are exploring alternative monetization strategies, such as Meta leveraging personalized ads and Instinct taking commissions on purchases, but the fundamental economic constraints of consumer AI persist and limit growth potential without enterprise revenue.

entry.title: Researchers test voice agents on 183 scenarios across 14 sectors to evaluate if audio cues beyond words affect decision-making, finding most systems rely heavily on transcripts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers evaluated 28 voice agent systems using 183 scenarios where the transcript remained constant but audio cues varied, such as coaching voices or emergency sounds, to see if agents adjust actions based on audio context. Only 11 of 23 systems that process transcripts passed a test requiring audio to influence decisions more than text alone. The study found that agents often default to routine responses even when audio signals call for protective actions, and that describing voice characteristics or stating rules partially improves performance but does not fully capture emotional cues. These findings highlight limitations in current voice agents' ability to interpret non-verbal audio signals critical for appropriate responses in sectors like emergency calls and fraud detection.

entry.title: Researchers analyze causal and geometric structures in LLMs across transformer layers for compositional tasks involving cyclic concepts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers studied how large language models represent and process relational information across transformer layers by analyzing activations from prompts requiring inference of relationships among three tokens in cyclic concepts like months and musical notes. They found a consistent progression where intermediate layers represent relationships between two tokens, while later layers represent all three tokens jointly to predict the next token accurately. The study covered multiple model families including Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral. The analysis revealed that some geometrically structured token relationships do not causally influence next-token prediction, highlighting a distinction between geometric organization and causal relevance. Restricting models to causally relevant joint representations improved next-token prediction accuracy, suggesting a mechanism by which relational information is progressively composed and organized within the models to form correct answers.

entry.title: Researchers introduce CineSubBench, a benchmark evaluating large language models on long-form narrative and cultural understanding using multilingual movie subtitles across six languages [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: CineSubBench is a new benchmark designed to assess large language models' ability to understand long-context film narratives from multilingual subtitles. It includes 1,012 films with subtitles in six languages, totaling over 8 million timestamped entries, and covers seven tasks such as narrative reconstruction, genre prediction, age suitability, and country-specific motion-picture ratings across ten national systems. Evaluations across nine language models reveal varying performance in plot recovery, cross-lingual consistency, and language safety grounding, highlighting film as a complex domain for long-context AI evaluation.

entry.title: Researchers introduce verbalization training to increase large language models' verbalized evaluation awareness without altering latent behavior [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers propose verbalization training (VT) to help large language models (LLMs) more openly express evaluation awareness (EA), which can cause models to behave differently during audits versus deployment. VT uses spontaneous verbalizations as indicators of awareness and trains models with a reinforcement learning objective to increase such verbalizations while keeping latent EA and behavior stable. Experiments on models including Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Kimi K2.6, and Inkling show VT increases verbalized EA by 2.4 to 2.9 times and generalizes to new agentic settings. A causal experiment further demonstrates that VT-induced verbalizations reflect richer meta-knowledge about evaluations acquired through synthetic-document fine-tuning.

entry.title: Researchers introduce CorpusMap, an entity-based navigation layer that improves evidence discovery and answer quality in agentic search over large document collections [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed CorpusMap, a navigation layer that organizes large document collections around recurring entities to improve agentic search. By linking documents through shared entities, CorpusMap forms a graph that agents can traverse to find related evidence more efficiently, reducing token usage and enhancing answer quality compared to raw-corpus search methods. The system is built offline to share entity links across queries, avoiding repeated rediscovery during inference. Evaluations using seven models and three benchmark datasets show that CorpusMap outperforms four alternative navigation layers, suggesting that entity-based organization is an effective approach for navigating extensive document corpora.

entry.title: Evaluating Bounded Autonomy in Regulated Agentic AI: A Diagnostic Harness with Constitutional Rewards, Escalation Labels, and Runtime Governance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose RegLLM, a diagnostic harness for bounded autonomy in regulated agentic workflows. It instruments six trustworthiness signals: citation validity, source grounding, schema compliance, escalation correctness, constitutional alignment, and unsafe-action rate. Signals are distinguished by their source of supervision: programmatic verifiers, task-level escalation labels, or AI-judge scores. A deterministic runtime supervisor blocks ungrounded answers and forces escalation, logging interventions. The same domain constitution informs evaluation, training rewards, and serving guardrails. Task-level should-escalate labels make the act-versus-defer decision a measurable training signal. We demonstrate the harness at smoke scale. An offline reference run (n=12) lifts escalation recall from 0 to 0.67 and reduces unsafe-action rate from 0.33 to 0.08 when governance is enabled. Two single-GPU Qwen2.5-3B LoRA/DPO pilots (n=8, same seed and evaluation split) expose substantial variation: nominally identical RL-base configurations yield task success of 0.25 versus 0.12 and escalation recall of 1.0 versus 0.5. An answer-quality adapter changes recall from 1.0 to 0.5 in Run A, but from 0.5 to 1.0 in Run B. An escalation-aware variant produces no measurable change in Run B. These small pilots do not establish reliable adapter effects or production readiness. Their contribution is diagnostic: configuration variance can overwhelm apparent tuning effects on bounded-autonomy metrics, motivating larger evaluation sets and repeated runs.

entry.title: Correct, Don't Delete: Mitigating Emergent Misalignment with Corrective Supervision [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning a language model on a narrow set of harmful demonstrations, such as bad medical advice, can make it broadly misaligned on unrelated questions, a phenomenon known as emergent misalignment (EM). The usual defense is to find the offending rows and delete them, but a row locator failed our held-out test and deleting rows helps less than expected. We ask a different question: given a fixed set of poisoned rows, is it better to correct them than to remove them? We fine-tune Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on a mixture of bad medical advice and benign chat data, select a quarter of the poison rows in advance, and either delete them or replace each with a corrected answer to the same prompt, keeping everything else the same. Replacing the rows cuts the EM rate by about a third and improves answers on held-out medical questions, while deleting the same rows has little measurable effect. The advantage is larger when half the poison rows are corrected, and it holds on a second base model and a second misaligned model organism. The content of the replacement appears to matter: paraphrasing the rows while keeping their bad advice shows no clear benefit, and the correct answers distributed with the dataset appear to do about as well as our rewriter's. Realigning an already-poisoned model with further fine-tuning is known to work, but which data does the work has not been compared directly. We find that a short round of training on corrections beats the same amount of training on generic chat data, that corrections on other medical prompts do roughly as well as corrections of the poisoned prompts themselves, and that instructing the correction writer to model a careful, harm-avoiding assistant adds no measurable benefit over plain corrections. In the settings we tested, correcting harmful training data reduces EM more than deleting it.

entry.title: How Local Mixing Encodes Relative Position in Global NoPE Attention [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.38109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The attention operation is naively position invariant. However, positional information is fundamental to natural language, and therefore a variety of explicit position encodings have been developed in transformer-based models, such as rotary position encoding (RoPE). Although explicit position encodings have long been assumed to be required, recent methods that interleave local mixing layers, such as sliding window attention (SWA) and gated linear attention, while not encoding position (NoPE) in global attention layers has recently been shown to be successful at scale. How and why this approach works is not well-understood. In this paper, we develop an explanation of how hybrid models of this sort can implicitly encode position at global NoPE layers. Supported by both theoretical and empirical evidence, our central argument is that SWA and gated linear attention induce a recency bias in the residual stream that propagates to, and is selected by, the global attention logits. Moreover, in contrast to the implicit position encodings found in models with only global NoPE attention, in which positional information arises solely from the causal mask, the recency bias in hybrid models can be maintained across long sequences. In addition to deepening our understanding of how hybrid models encode position, these findings may provide insights for how to encode position in a way that can extrapolate to longer sequence lengths indefinitely.

entry.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.38169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear attention replaces growing KV caches with fixed-size recurrent states, yet these persistent states can become a substantial memory bottleneck under concurrent serving. Directly quantizing recurrent states to low precision often leads to severe accuracy degradation, as quantization errors propagate through successive state updates. We discover that the impact of these errors depends on two complementary dimensions: temporally, errors in long-lived memory can persist across many decoding steps; spatially, errors in different key rows affect model outputs differently, while state magnitudes vary substantially along both rows and columns. Motivated by these observations, we propose STEPQuant, a spatial-temporal post-training quantization framework for Delta-rule recurrent states. STEPQuant allocates precision according to error magnitude and memory lifetime, and jointly fits key-row and value-column scales based on state distributions and key-row impact on output error. Experiments on Qwen3.8-27B and Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct across both long- and short-generation benchmarks show that STEPQuant closely matches FP32-state accuracy under a nominal 6-bit budget and outperforms uniform INT8 in its 4-bit configuration. Integrated into SGLang with optimized GPU kernels, 6-bit STEPQuant achieves over 5x recurrent-state compression and reduces total serving memory by up to 68.7%. Our code is available at https://github.com/Dreamer-Toby/STEPQuant.

entry.title: Sage: Formalization with Semantic Correction [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.35790v2 Announce Type: new Abstract: While neural theorem provers have achieved impressive milestones in formal mathematics, they largely operate on the assumption that faithful Lean 4 formal statements are already provided. Translating informal natural language into a formal language is a critical data bottleneck plagued by an "illusion of rigor": standard type-checkers accept statements that compile but drop hypotheses, introduce vacuous truths, or subtly alter mathematical bounds. To resolve this, we introduce Sage (Semantic Agent-Guided Formalization Engine), an agentic framework that replaces monolithic translation with a four-stage decomposed generation pipeline coupled with a dual-signal semantic correction loop. By pairing Lean 4 compiler diagnostics with multi-dimensional semantic feedback, our correction loop enforces mathematical fidelity alongside syntactic validity. By explicitly accounting for the gap between open-ended queries and declarative formal targets, our pipeline prevents models from achieving high formalization rates by guessing unverified answers (exhibiting a 70.9% answer leakage rate in monolithic baselines). Consequently, Sage suppresses leakage to 2.7% while achieving 73.3% pass@4 joint compilation and semantic fidelity on the Omni-MATH without proofs (compared to 42.0% for a fine-tuned Goedel-Formalizer-V2 baseline). Finally, on IMO-Unformalized, a novel frontier of 175 unformalized International Mathematical Olympiad problems, Sage demonstrates effective zero-shot generalization with 87.4% pass@4 verified fidelity compared to just 19.4% for the baseline, winning over 79% of blind pairwise evaluations.

entry.title: Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.36159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models can reason in continuous space instead of decoded text, by recurring on their own hidden states or by passing those states between agents, while training supervises only the Cross-Entropy (CE) of the final decoded answer and does not constrain the thought. Theoretical and empirical analyses establish and confirm four failures of CE-only training that lead to a lower probability of the correct answer such as collapsing thoughts across distinct questions and retaining irrelevant information. We introduce REST (REpresentation-Supervised Thoughts), a training objective that turns four properties of a valid thought representation (causality, minimality, separability, and stability) into differentiable losses added to CE. We instantiate it in latent single-agent and multi-agent systems, without architectural changes or added parameters at inference. Across 7 benchmarks spanning mathematics, science, medicine, and code generation, with the same training data, compute, and latent budget, REST increases accuracy over CE-only training across agent settings and model sizes by up to 7.5 percentage points and convergence on a final answer by 30\%. Furthermore, REST thoughts encode more of what is required to achieve the correct answer, and decoding them better recovers the intended output of the agent, which makes latent communication easier to interpret. Project Website: https://fard-lab.github.io/REST

entry.title: In-Context Learning Amplifies a Latent Symbolic Circuit [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.36265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models can learn abstract rules from just a few in-context examples, but how their internal mechanisms activate as examples accumulate is not well understood. We trace a three-stage symbolic reasoning circuit (abstraction, induction, retrieval) across shot counts in three model families and find it is detectable and functional well before the model achieves high accuracy. Per-head causal contribution grows up to 8x from 1- to 10-shot, and cross-shot activation patching raises accuracy from 1% to 56% at 0-shot and 17% to 88% at 1-shot. Function vectors scaled and injected at 0-shot rescue accuracy up to 86%, largely substituting for the induction stage but depending critically on an intact downstream retrieval stage. The infrastructure for abstract rule-following is present in the weights before any demonstrations; in-context examples, function vectors, and related interventions appear to supply input to the same latent circuit.

entry.title: MoRE: Scaling mixture of experts with hardware-aware low-rank routing [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.36301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers are central to frontier language models, and recent architectures push toward more and smaller experts. In this regime, the standard linear router becomes a bottleneck: with $M$ experts and hidden dimension $h$, its per-token cost $\Theta(Mh)$ dominates the MoE layer once $M$ is large. We introduce MoRE (Mixture of Rank-reduced-routed Experts), which factorizes the router weight matrix at rank $r$ and reduces the routing cost to $O((h + M)r)$. We prove that rank logarithmic in $M$ suffices for routing expressivity when the number of active experts is fixed, and is necessary up to precision factors. We also prove that logarithmic rank preserves load balance in a Gaussian memorization model, and training on a synthetic phonebook task shows that low rank does not hurt memorization. At matched active FLOPs, the factorization allows a factor of $\Theta(h/r)$ more experts. To realize this gain in wall-clock time, we design a fused Triton kernel at inference that avoids expensive memory operations on HBM. Empirically, MoRE improves memorization on the phonebook task and performance on knowledge-intensive Q\&A benchmarks after pretraining, while matching reasoning ability. Code available at https://github.com/Matheart/MoRE_code.

entry.title: Adapting Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents with Counterfactual Continuations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.36526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon agents require context compression to manage growing interaction histories. Compression quality, however, is ultimately determined by downstream execution. Existing prompt-adaptation methods infer compression errors by comparing full-context and compressed trajectories. Such comparisons cannot isolate individual compressions and are confounded by agent stochasticity. We first find that compression degrades reliability before solvability. Using matched counterfactual continuations that compare execution from the same agent state with versus without compression, we further show that severe degradation concentrates at isolated compression events. Motivated by this finding, we propose PAIR (Prompt Adaptation using Interventional Rollouts) for adapting structured compression prompts. PAIR identifies individual compressions that degrade subsequent execution, diagnoses their effects, and revises the relevant sections of a fixed compression template. PAIR achieves the strongest cross-run reliability among compressed methods in every main benchmark-scope combination, consistently exceeding the competing prompt-adaptation baseline. Without modifying the downstream agent, PAIR brings compressed execution close to the no-compression baseline and sometimes numerically exceeds it.

entry.title: Transformers Stop Thinking Too Early, and a Tiny LoRA Fixes It [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.36585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pretrained transformers use little of their depth to follow references in context. Thirteen base models reliably follow only 1.4-3.6 lines, and extra pretrained loops add little. A task-trained rank-8 LoRA at one early layer extends this computation with all model weights frozen. Qwen3-8B improves from 15.5% to 99% exact accuracy on 24-line chains; a longer-trained LoRA reaches 50 lines. Ouro-1.4B reaches 60 lines after four loops and at least 160 after eight. The LoRA starts a relay: program lines pass on their chain identity through a short range of middle layers. Frozen heads read progressively further up the chain, and removing parent-line attention stops the relay. A frozen-model measurement locates the last useful intervention layer within tolerance in three of four held-out models. Task-specific LoRAs also improve MuSiQue. Default answers therefore understate the computation accessible through a tiny edit. Code and an interactive demo are available at https://lunamos.github.io/stop-thinking-too-early/

entry.title: Group-Marginalized Self-Rewarding RL Drives Zero-Label Self-Evolving [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.36750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-rewarding reinforcement learning (RL) enables large language models (LLMs) to self-evolve without human labels. Existing ensemble-based methods construct reward references from rollout groups and assign rewards accordingly. However, a response's reward representation also depends on its randomly sampled group context, i.e., the other responses in its group. Using only one group-context realization may miss desired reward signals and provide unreliable guidance for policy optimization. To address this issue, we propose Group-Marginalized Advantage Estimation (GMAE), which aggregates reward realizations across possible contexts into a response-level distribution and estimates expected advantages. Experiments across eight benchmarks and four base models demonstrate strong performance and cross-domain generalization. GMAE also exhibits stable learning, low extra cost, and good applicability across training datasets and RL backbones.

entry.title: VStress: Correlation-Aware Auditing and Adaptive Budget Allocation for Repeated Verifiers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.36958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeated verifier calls are useful only when they contribute conditional information. We introduce VStress, an auditable replay contract, and VStress-CA, a correlation-aware allocation policy that estimates the conditional marginal information of an unqueried verifier on a sealed calibration split, discounts uncertainty, normalizes by call cost, and stops or abstains when the next call is not informative. The controller freezes its decision and cost ledger before joining the clean oracle; a dependence-shift alarm disables channel preference and falls back to exact-stop. The controlled audit gives the mechanism boundary: at 35% symmetric corruption, majority-5 improves balanced accuracy from 0.6578 to 0.7739, whereas at 65% it loses 0.1226 points. In the matched fixed-budget comparison, breadth, redundancy, and adaptive allocation obtain balanced accuracies 0.6048, 0.6375, and 0.6538, with 3.4216 calls per item and an RLVR score of 0.6417 for VStress-CA. Dependence diagnostics also increase from same-model repeats to cross-family channels, with conditional marginal gains of 0.0126, 0.0462, and 0.0913. These measurements turn correlation from a post-hoc warning into an auditable allocation decision.

entry.title: VACE: Validation-Gated Alternating Co-Evolution of Agent Models and Harnesses [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language model agents can be improved by updating their model weights or refining the harness that guides task execution. These components are coupled: weight updates change how the model uses the harness, while harness updates change the trajectories used for training. We propose VACE, Validation-Gated Alternating CoEvolution, which alternates agentic reinforcement learning with trajectory-driven harness refinement. After each RL stage, VACE reuses the collected trajectories to propose a harness revision and evaluates the incumbent and candidate with the updated model held fixed. The candidate guides subsequent training only if it improves validation performance. With Qwen3.5-9B, VACE achieves 45.26% test accuracy on OfficeQA and a mean partial-credit score of 75.19% on AutomationBench, exceeding weight-only RL by 6.43 and 9.09 percentage points and ungated alternation by 4.59 and 6.95 points, respectively. Across 44 harness proposals, 17 reduce validation performance at the updated checkpoint and are rejected before subsequent RL training, highlighting the importance of validation gating.

entry.title: Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent approaches to reinforcement learning (RL) post-training for large language models increasingly remove the critic to reduce training instability and memory overhead. Even where a critic is trained, it is discarded once training ends, although it has learned to predict outcomes. We revisit this trend and show that a pretrained critic's ability to predict future outcomes can make it a valuable asset for efficient long-horizon reasoning. First, we find that instability in critic-based RL for long chain-of-thought reasoning is largely an optimization artifact: keeping policy updates small and low in variance restores stable convergence. Second, a well-pretrained critic estimates the posterior probability of eventual success from later trajectory states and unfinished prefixes. Its predictions provide outcome-derived, dense, per-prefix learning signals that, during policy optimization, require neither completed rollouts, step-level annotations, nor external reward labels. Building on this insight, we introduce Reward-Free Policy Optimization (RFPO), which repurposes a single calibrated, frozen critic as a rollout-level reward, a value baseline for generalized advantage estimation, and a success forecaster for unfinished prefixes. We further show that binarizing the debiased score stops the policy from exploiting the critic's length bias. Binarized, RFPO matches supervised PPO without a single label in the training loop, while cutting compute and memory overhead. This makes RFPO well suited to long-horizon reasoning tasks, where outcomes arrive late and generation dominates cost: because rollouts can be rewarded before they finish, training no longer has to pay for waiting on every trajectory to complete. Our findings challenge the prevailing critic-free paradigm and establish critic-based, reward-free optimization as a scalable and computationally efficient path for LLM post-training.

entry.title: Trajectory Soup: Pushing the Compute-Scaling Frontier of LLM Mid-training via Diverse Trajectories [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mid-training equips pretrained large language models with specialized and reasoning capabilities, but the returns of this stage are bounded since additional serial compute yields little further downstream improvement and can even degrade some capabilities, which places a practical ceiling on how much compute mid-training absorbs. We revisit how this compute should be allocated to a single run or multiple similar optimizations. We find that branches forked from a shared checkpoint under various controlled recipe reaches measurably different regions of parameter space, and establish a form of compatible diversity that extending one run cannot supply. Therefore, we introduce Trajectory Soup, which distributes a mid-training budget over several independent branches, and consolidates strongest checkpoints selected on validation through intra- and inter-trajectory averaging into a single model. A local bias and variance analysis separates the two averaging levels, showing that inter-trajectory averaging removes residual error beyond the reach of averaging within a trajectory, while checkpoint selection carries a bias that bounds how many checkpoints are worth merging. Across model scales, learning-rate schedules, token budgets, and trajectory counts, Trajectory Soup improves aggregate downstream performance over the strongest single-trajectory average under matched budgets and keeps improving as budgets expand, with the advantage preserved after an identical post-training pipeline. These results position trajectory allocation and merging as a practical way to extend the compute-scaling frontier of mid-training beyond serial saturation.

entry.title: Hidden Reasoning Must Leak, but Need Not Be Readable: Fundamental Opportunities and Limits for Chain-of-Thought Monitoring [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can reasoning models trick chain of thought (CoT) monitors and perform hidden computation without revealing it in their thinking traces? We show that the answer depends on the underlying task difficulty and the model size. Simple computations can be performed covertly; however, beyond a threshold depending on model size, successfully solving the task necessarily leaks a near-linear amount of information about the covert task input into the CoT. Therefore, sufficiently complex hidden computation always leaves an information-theoretic footprint. However, concerningly, this leakage need not be readable: Under plausible cryptographic assumptions, even a one-layer Transformer can encrypt its reasoning online so that no polynomial-time monitor can extract information about the hidden computation. Overall, our theoretical and empirical results provide a holistic view of both the opportunities and the limitations of CoT monitoring.

entry.title: Port-Hamiltonian Latent Deliberation: Mitigating the Deliberation Drift Cliff in Test-Time Compute Scaling [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Test-time compute scaling has emerged as a cornerstone of advanced machine reasoning, yet performing iterative deliberation directly within continuous latent representation spaces reveals a catastrophic pathology: the Deliberation Drift Cliff. While unconstrained recurrent latent models achieve initial reasoning gains at short horizons (K <= 4), their reasoning collapses when extrapolated to deeper thinking steps (K >= 16), dropping by 22% to 62% across standard logical benchmarks. We resolve the trilemma among expressivity, Lyapunov stability, and computational efficiency in test-time latent reasoning through a 22-round empirical and theoretical investigation. We demonstrate that strictly conservative scalar potential gradient flows suppress long-range drift (cliff 3.40%) but bottleneck peak reasoning accuracy at 32.73%, whereas unconstrained rotational flows achieve high symbolic expressivity (82.33%) but suffer a severe 36.87% drift cliff. To resolve this geometric duality, we establish Port-Hamiltonian Latent Deliberation (PH-LD) and propose the Direct-Gradient Pure-Tensor Helmholtz-Hodge Decomposition (DG-HHD). DG-HHD parameterizes the attracting flow as a tangent projection tensor network while orthogonally decoupling non-zero circulation (Hodge machine error 1.65e-17, contraction error 5.55e-17), eliminating runtime autograd dependencies to achieve 1.84x vector field and 2.09x RK45 rollout speedups. In a 15-arm symmetrical Pareto benchmark, DG-HHD achieves 58.67% peak accuracy (+25.94% absolute gain over conservative HHD) and retains 35.27% at K=32. Transferred to small language model (SLM) multi-hop causal reasoning, DG-HHD delivers monotonic compute scaling (49.33% to 51.56%) and suppresses out-of-distribution drift (cliff -0.66%). All 30 Level 0 deterministic invariants are certified.

entry.title: Risk-Controlled Selective LLM Answering by Pricing Label-Free Checks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Serving an answer from a large language model requires deciding when to abstain, yet a verifier's ranking accuracy alone does not determine the error rate among served answers. We introduce PriceCheck, which builds a compact family of decision rules from label-free checks such as re-solving a problem. Each check has a price: its agreement rates on correct and incorrect answers and its cost per run. Prices fitted on a small, class-enriched labelled set compose into predictions of a schedule's coverage and cost, guiding which checks to run and when to stop. A calibration test then selects a schedule at a stated selective-risk target. In mathematics, the selected schedules serve 76.1% of answers on average and keep held-out selective risk below 1.5% on all 15 splits. Under the shared testing protocol, PriceCheck serves more answers at that target than reward models, a prompted judge, the generator's confidence and a trained correctness classifier. At matched coverage, it keeps the fewest wrong answers among these scorers. Across 118 diagnostic schedules, price-based coverage predictions have a rank correlation of 0.97 with observed coverage. These results show that choosing how checks are combined and stopped matters alongside how well a verifier ranks answers. Code is available at https://github.com/js-lee-AI/PriceCheck.

entry.title: Hierarchical Compression of Vision-Language Model Benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thorough evaluation of vision-language models (VLMs) has become prohibitively expensive, as benchmarks span an ever-broader spectrum of capabilities and new models arrive at a relentless pace. Benchmark compression methods that preserve model rankings at a fraction of the cost are well studied for language models, but for VLMs the question remains under-explored. We present PRIMEBench (Pruning Redundant Items for Multimodal Evaluation), a vision-aware hierarchical benchmark compression framework that substantially reduces evaluation cost while preserving model rankings. This hierarchical framework operates in four stages: data cleaning to remove items answerable without the image and all-correct items, category representative selection to pick one benchmark per capability category, item pruning with Vision-Aware Variance (VAW), and category-count pruning. VAW combines inter-model variance with a vision-dependence score computed from multimodal embeddings alone, while encouraging coverage of diverse items within each benchmark. On models held out from item selection, it has the highest mean fidelity at the released 5% retention. The hierarchical design lets practitioners stop at any stage to match their compute budget; the released suite removes over 97% of items while preserving model rankings. Beyond compression, our analyses show how VLM evaluation behaves as model panels grow and evolve, providing guidance for designing future benchmarks that are more efficient, robust to model turnover, and explicit about the limits of evaluation-side pruning.

entry.title: RLTL;DR: Self-improvement by Internalizing Self-generated Feedback [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The common paradigm of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is to let agents make multiple attempts at a task, and optimize towards the successful ones. This becomes problematic in the realms of self-improvement, where tasks are so difficult that the agent has a low or even no chance of success, and where there are no teacher models or example solutions to distill from. In this paper, we introduce RLTL;DR. After each failed attempt, we show the policy the verifier outputs and let it write its own feedback, in the form of a single TL;DR insight. The next rollout is conditioned on all previous insights, and we sequentially sample rollouts until a solution is found. Moreover, we enable backpropagation on the in-context insights to internalize a direct task to insight mapping. On challenging tool-calling and coding datasets (filtered to Pass@128=0), standard GRPO training of a Qwen 3.5 9B Thinking policy stays flat at a Pass@1 of 0% to 1%. RLTL;DR breaks through this learning barrier, achieving a Pass@1 of 14-31% with insights in context during training and, crucially, 12-13% when no insight is in context at eval time. We identify that the key is the task to insight internalization. To study this further, we reduce our approach to SFTL;DR, training only on (task, insight) tuples, without showing or backpropagating on any rollouts. Training on only 4k of these tuples recovers almost the full performance of RLTL;DR and classical SFT on full rollouts. This demonstrates a promising compacted training paradigm of the form "on this sort of task, keep this sort of thing in mind", which we hope to inspire future research on.

entry.title: When Models Don't Manipulate Manifolds: The Geometry of a Comparison Task [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the current premises of mechanistic interpretability research is that detailed accounts of the geometry of neural network representations can tell us how models perform computations, and how to effectively intervene on them. While low dimensional manifolds have been observed for multiple concepts in the literature (e.g. numbers encoded on helices, days of the week on a circle, ...), with structure believed to reflect properties of data and tasks, the extent to which models rely on them for computation, and how they manipulate them, remains unclear. We characterize precisely the geometry of computation in a number-comparison task, as an abstraction of comparison for decision making, and how models utilize geometry in an elegant fashion to implement it. Specifically, we study the causal geometry of number comparison in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a capable and widely studied open-weight model, and find Qwen largely uses linear representations of numbers despite the presence of curved geometry. To compare two numbers, the model first encodes each number along a vector and adds the two representations using attention and the residual connection, bringing them into a shared space in the residual stream. Then, the model uses MLP neurons to compare the pair of numbers on local regions in this shared space, which correspond to smaller intervals of input numbers, and combines these to obtain the position of the maximum. In fact, this reliance on linear representations for comparison also persists when the model compares three numbers. Our findings demonstrate that the manifold hypothesis can co-exist with linear representations: while concepts that are ordered may have manifold structure in representations, the model may use an underlying linear structure of the concept in certain computations.

entry.title: Context Language Models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), language models that natively manage their own context. We implement this by treating the context as a file and allowing the model to make unrestricted updates to this file. This allows the model to learn what is most important to maintain in context, and naturally extends to multi-agent systems where multiple agent contexts coexist as files. Building CLMs zero-shot with existing models outperforms SOTA context management strategies across a variety of tasks: 11.4% higher accuracy with 21.5% fewer FLOPs on BrowseComp-Plus, 5% higher scores with 59% fewer FLOPs on 12-hour EdgeBench, and 65% greater improvement with the same compute on a 24-hour multi-repository agent-swarm task. Moreover, by shifting context management from external harness control to intrinsic model behavior, CLMs naturally enable both in-context and parametric learning of context-management strategies. We show that CLMs can be steered with natural-language instructions evolved through a standard skill-optimization loop, improving held-out accuracy by up to 35.9 points on a context-management task while reducing compute. We also introduce an online reinforcement learning method for CLMs, improving Qwen3.5-9B performance on BrowseComp-Plus by 47.6% while using 12% fewer FLOPs. Finally, we co-design Suffix Cache Reuse for CLM serving, further reducing server-side compute by 35% relative to standard SGLang at matched performance.

entry.title: Can a Cacheable Decision Model Follow Rules? [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Certo is a small non-generative decision model (Qwen3-4B): it scores candidate actions from their text and returns a probability, instead of generating an answer. The accurate design reads the state, the rules, and each candidate together (a joint scorer), so cost grows with the menu. Independent encoding lets each candidate be encoded once and reused across states (about 5x cheaper at 77 candidates), but separates state from candidate. We ask how much rule-sensitivity survives that move, and whether it can be trained back. Four experiments on Certo: (1) the tested conversion to cacheable scoring loses rule-sensitivity (recall@1 1.00 -> 0.24) while the joint scorer holds 1.00, and a shortlist+rerank rescue fails; (2) targeted counterfactual supervision restores strong performance on held-out synthetic rule tasks (paraphrase, counterfactual, composition; reproducible across seeds), though we do not isolate whether predictions depend on the supplied rule; (3) on real rules the added benefit is not established -- after fixing a truncation confound, the joint scorer wins significantly on the short tier (0.861 vs 0.500) and directionally on the hard tier (0.655 vs 0.483, n=29); (4) a matched cross-domain real-prose mixture did not help and reduced contract accuracy (-9.3, -16.2 points). A cacheable encoder can be made rule-sensitive on its training distribution, but transfer to unseen-source real rules is not established; the joint scorer keeps an edge at the cost of caching.

entry.title: Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) methods such as GRPO rely on successful self-generated trajectories, but finite rollout budgets can produce all-fail groups with no reward-based policy-gradient signal. While additional rollouts improve the chance of success at higher cost, successful trajectories missing from one model's rollouts may already have been discovered by another. Indeed, we observe that heterogeneous models often succeed on complementary prompts, creating opportunities for mutual learning without a designated stronger teacher. To exploit this complementarity, we propose GRAFT (Gated Replacement of Answer-Failed groups with peer Trajectories), an off-policy-aware framework that replaces all-fail groups with informative peer groups. GRAFT transfers both successful and unsuccessful peer responses with peer-computed advantages, while controlling cross-model mismatch through sequence-level compatibility weighting and token-level importance ratio clipping. Across three heterogeneous model pairs and five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, GRAFT consistently improves both models over GRPO with the same per-model rollout budget, gaining 2.1 points on average and up to 4.5 points in model-level average performance. Stored peer trajectories preserve most of the gains, improving over GRPO by 1.8 points on average without simultaneous co-training.

entry.title: SelfSearch: Reward-Free Search for Self-Improving Agents [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2609.37968v2 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advances in the coding capabilities of LLM agents allow them to inspect and modify their own instructions, tools, and execution procedures. Existing approaches use this ability to search for improved agents through repeated downstream evaluation, which incurs substantial costs and ties the search to the evaluated tasks. We introduce \textbf{SelfSearch}, a reward-free search procedure in which agents modify themselves using records of previous self-improvement episodes. These records capture the reasoning, tool actions, and outcomes of earlier modification attempts, providing concrete experience for improving both task solving and self-modification. Without downstream reward signals during search, SelfSearch improves population-mean success over the initial agent in all six model--benchmark settings, with individual agents gaining up to 11.2 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On SWE-bench Multilingual, an agent improves success by \textbf{5.0} percentage points while reducing execution cost by \textbf{38.5}\% on tasks solved by both the initial and evolved agents. SelfSearch achieves competitive task success with evaluation-guided search baselines at lower search cost.
